children: President Donald Trump thanked Lockheed Martin
CEO Jim Taiclet on Monday as the White House inaugurated a new granite heliport designed to accommodate the latest generation of Marine One helicopters.

Trump said in a Truth Social post that he had taken the maiden flight from the newly completed heliport and credited Taiclet with making a “valuable contribution” to the project. Trump also thanked construction workers, stone masons and Clark Construction, which supervised the work.

, through its Sikorsky helicopter business, helped fund the project. Trump previously said Sikorsky would spend about $5 million to $6 million on the landing pad. Lockheed confirmed that its contribution was made to the National Park Service.
The cost of the heliport is immaterial relative to Lockheed’s overall business, making Monday's announcement unlikely to have a meaningful direct effect on earnings or valuation.

The project does, however, draw attention to Sikorsky's role in one of the company's most visible government programs. Sikorsky manufactures the VH-92A Patriot, the newest presidential helicopter used as Marine One when the president is aboard.

The aircraft were formally delivered to the U.S. Marine Corps in 2024 as part of a roughly $5 billion program to replace the aging presidential helicopter fleet. The newer helicopters had faced an unusual operational problem at the White House: their powerful exhaust could damage the South Lawn.
The permanent landing area was intended to solve that problem and allow the newer aircraft to operate routinely from the White House grounds.

Trump said in July that Sikorsky would cover roughly $5 million to $6 million of the cost. Lockheed said its contribution was being made through the National Park Service and was conducted in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
For investors, that expenditure is negligible for a company the size of Lockheed. The more notable aspect may be the public recognition of Taiclet and Lockheed
by the president at a time when the U.S. government remains by far the defense contractor's most important customer.

The project also puts Sikorsky's VH-92A back in the spotlight after the aircraft's transition into presidential service encountered delays partly because of concerns about its exhaust damaging the White House lawn.

Construction began in June and underwent modifications after Trump raised concerns about the appearance and slope of the landing area. Clark Construction supervised the project, which was accelerated ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping's planned state visit this week.

Monday's opening therefore removes a highly visible, if financially minor, operational obstacle for the Sikorsky presidential helicopter fleet. It isn't a new defense contract or a material revenue event for Lockheed
, but it marks another step toward fuller use of the VH-92A at the White House.

title: Trump thanks Lockheed Martin CEO as new White House heliport opens
